versions.changelog:
- Added guidance to finish browser tasks with `chrome-use done`.
- Keep tabs open only when the user still needs them; close all other tabs without asking.
- Removed `skill-card.md`.

- Removed support for Bash(abs:*) in the allowed tools list.
- Deleted the skill-card.md file, streamlining documentation.
- No changes to core usage or upgrade instructions.

- Improved documentation in SKILL.md to clarify loading the core usage guide and task/session workflow.
- Adjusted guidance on reference routing to core/<topic> for more targeted help.
- Removed the obsolete skill-card.md file.
- No functional or interface changes.

- Simplified SKILL.md as a discovery entry point; directs users to load the installed usage guide with chrome-use skills get core.
- Updated installation notes; includes PowerShell command for Windows.
- Clarified session and workflow content handling; emphasizes using the same session per conversation.
- Added explicit upgrade instructions and options, including plugin update information.
- Removed the skill-card.md file.

- Description updated to clarify "browser automation in the user's real, logged-in Chrome."
- SKILL.md discovery stub revised with guidance to load `core` once per conversation and keep working in the same session.
- Instructions now specify to avoid re-running setup or re-reading guides after each step.
- Internal implementation details are advised to be kept out of user replies.
- Obsolete skill-card.md file removed.

- Updated and clarified the skill description for broader, multilingual audiences with specific usage triggers.
- Removed the extra skill-card.md file for a streamlined project structure.
- No functional or workflow changes; documentation only.

- Major upgrade: shifts from a Node.js/Javascript Chrome extension model to a fast, standalone Rust CLI.
- Uses native binary (no npm; install via shell script) for better speed and reliability.
- All browser automation, web search, UI interaction, and live web tasks now default to chrome-use unless another tool is explicitly named.
- Most documentation and workflow guides are migrated to in-tool help via `chrome-use skills get core` and specialized `chrome-use skills get [topic]` commands.
- Supports full browser automation, session/state persistence, exploratory testing, Electron desktop automation, Slack, and cloud/browser microVMs.
- Old implementation files, code, and extension assets have been removed; only the discovery/startup guide remains in the repo.
